subject: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

Hi Sofia/Laura/Rishi,

We need a customer-facing throughput SLO clause we can include in Dedicated order forms (and reference in the MSA/SLA addendum where applicable). Sales is getting consistent asks to “put the throughput guarantee in writing,” especially for Premium.

Can you please review/mark up the attached draft (v3) for:
- Contract-safe definition of the throughput commitment (what we guarantee + measurement window)
- Clear exclusions (customer-side throttles, unsupported models/versions, warmup, etc.)
- Remedies / credits language (and any caps / guardrails)

My goal is to finalize wording by EOW so we can unblock PM-503 and enablement.

Open questions I’d love guidance on:
1) Should we define throughput as tokens/sec (aggregated) or “requests that meet the customer’s configured max_tokens”? SRE strongly prefers tokens/sec.
2) Can we keep remedies as service credits only (no termination right) for Standard/Plus?
3) Do we want “commercially reasonable efforts” anywhere, or is that too squishy?

Thanks,
Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Dedicated_Throughput_SLO_Contract_Language_v3.docx
- Dedicated_SLO_Credit_Policy_Draft_2025-02-12.pdf


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

Lauren — skimmed v3 + credit policy draft.

Finance comments (high-level):
- Please keep credits tied to the monthly committed fee for the Dedicated deployment (not total spend / not blended across other products).
- We should cap total credits at 10% of the monthly committed fee per month for Standard/Plus. Premium can go higher if Legal is comfortable, but we need an explicit cap.
- The measurement needs to exclude customer-induced idle time / throttling, otherwise this can be gamed (e.g., a customer sends a handful of long requests and claims underperformance).
- Please avoid wording that implies we’re guaranteeing a particular model’s absolute tokens/sec under any prompt/context. We should anchor on “supported model versions” and “supported configuration ranges” (max context length, max output tokens).

If you want, I can propose specific credit table bands once we align on the metric.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
Finance (Pricing & Margin)
Redwood Inference


From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 12:27 PM PST
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

+1 to Laura.

A couple specifics I’d like included:
- Define the commitment as an “aggregate throughput floor” over a rolling window (e.g., 30 minutes), measured at the Redwood ingress, and only during “Eligible Minutes.” Otherwise we’ll be debating request mix and bursty patterns.
- Exclusion for “customer request parameters outside the supported range” needs to be explicit. We can list examples: context length beyond max for the shape/tier; forcing a non-default sampling config that materially impacts performance; and using experimental model versions not in the supported catalog.
- Credit trigger should require that the deployment is provisioned at the contracted shape and region (no credits if they voluntarily move regions or use a smaller shape temporarily).

If Legal is fine, I’d also add “sole and exclusive remedy” language around credits.

Rishi

—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A
Redwood Inference


From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 3:46 PM PST
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

Thanks, Lauren. I reviewed v3.

Legal notes / edits (summary):

1) Define terms up front
- “Dedicated Deployment” (deployment_id scoped)
- “Committed Throughput” (numeric floor stated in the Order Form; add unit: tokens/sec)
- “Eligible Minutes” (minutes in which: (a) deployment is in ‘Ready’ state, (b) customer sends requests above a minimum activity threshold, (c) no customer-side throttling / misconfiguration)
- “Throughput Shortfall” calculation should reference Redwood’s measurement system of record.

2) Avoid overpromising on model performance
- The guarantee should be contingent on “Supported Model(s)” and “Supported Configuration Range(s)” as defined in Redwood docs / order form.
- Recommend adding: “Customer acknowledges that throughput may vary by model architecture and request characteristics; Redwood’s commitment is limited to Committed Throughput as measured below.”

3) Exclusions
- Add explicit exclusion for: scheduled maintenance (with notice), emergency maintenance, beta/preview features, and Force Majeure.
- Add explicit exclusion for: customer prompts or parameters that violate our acceptable use / safety policy and get rate-limited or blocked.

4) Remedies
- OK to keep as service credits as the sole remedy.
- I strongly recommend a cap and to tie to the monthly committed fee for the impacted Dedicated Deployment (consistent with Laura’s note).
- For Premium customers, if Sales insists on “termination right,” we should route through deal desk / counsel review rather than bake into the standard language.

5) “Commercially reasonable efforts”
- Not needed here if we already have a defined commitment + credits remedy. It can weaken the promise and create interpretive ambiguity.

If you want, I can send redlines directly, but simplest is for you to incorporate the above and I’ll do a final pass.

Sofia

—
Sofia Mendes
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 10:14 AM PST
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

Super helpful, thank you.

Proposed decisions to confirm:
- Metric: tokens/sec (aggregate) measured at Redwood ingress, scoped to deployment_id
- Window: rolling 30 minutes
- Only count “Eligible Minutes” (deployment Ready + minimum activity threshold + customer not throttling)
- Remedy: service credits only; cap 10% of monthly committed fee for Standard/Plus; Premium TBD (default to 15% cap unless deal desk exception)

Two questions before I update the doc:
1) Minimum activity threshold: SRE suggested “>= 10k output tokens generated in the rolling window” to avoid low-traffic noise. Is that contract-safe, or should we define it more generally (“minimum usage threshold as specified by Redwood”)?
2) For exclusions, do we want to list examples in the contract, or keep as a shorter clause and point to docs? (My bias: list the big ones explicitly, point to docs for the rest.)

I’ll fold these into v4 and send for quick approval.

Lauren


From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 1:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

1) Activity threshold: I’d avoid hardcoding a specific token count in the contract unless we’re confident it won’t change. Better:
- Define “Eligible Minutes” to exclude periods where usage is below a “minimum usage threshold” and then specify that threshold in the Order Form (or an exhibit) that we can update with mutual agreement.
- Alternatively, define it as “Customer must submit sufficient traffic to reasonably measure throughput” and keep the exact threshold in our internal SLO doc. The risk is customers asking “what is sufficient,” so I prefer Order Form / exhibit.

2) Exclusions: list the key ones explicitly in the contract (throttling, unsupported configs, maintenance, force majeure). Keep the rest as a general “including but not limited to” + cross-reference the Dedicated Documentation.

Also: please include a sentence that we measure at the service boundary (Redwood ingress) and that customer-side networking issues are excluded.

Sofia


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 4:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO language for Dedicated MSAs / Order Forms (Standard/Plus/Premium)

Implemented updates in v4 (not re-attaching to avoid version confusion — changes are in the working doc in Drive and I’ll publish the final after your go-ahead).

What I changed:
- Added definitions: Dedicated Deployment, Committed Throughput, Eligible Minutes, Supported Model(s), Supported Configuration Range(s)
- Measurement: aggregate output tokens/sec at Redwood ingress over rolling 30-minute window, computed only across Eligible Minutes
- Minimum activity threshold moved to Order Form exhibit (blank field for now). Wording: “as specified in the Order Form.”
- Exclusions: customer-side throttling and misconfiguration; unsupported models/configs; customer networking issues; scheduled/emergency maintenance; beta/preview; force majeure; AUP-triggered rate limits/blocks
- Remedies: service credits are sole and exclusive remedy; cap at 10% (Standard/Plus) and 15% (Premium default)

If you (Sofia) can confirm the revised structure is OK, I’ll:
1) send the final clause to Elliot/Docs for alignment with public Dedicated tier docs,
2) update PM-503 with the approved language,
3) sync with Sales Enablement so they stop promising “per-request TPS guarantees.”

Thanks all — this unblocks a bunch.

Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
